artists.biography: HIM is a Finnish rock band from Helsinki. Formed in 1991 by vocalist Ville Valo, guitarist Mikko "Linde" Lindström, and bassist Mikko "Migé" Paananen, HIM's current lineup consists of Valo, Linde, Migé, Janne "Emerson Burton" Puurtinen on keyboards and Mika Karppinen on drums. They have released seven full-length albums to date and are currently working on their eighth, titled Tears on Tape, to be released in 2013. On September 5, 2006, HIM's fifth studio album Dark Light was certified gold by the RIAA, making HIM the first Finnish band to have a gold album in the United States. HIM had five of their studio albums certified platinum in Finland with Razorblade Romance being certified double platinum in Finland and platinum in Germany.

Released in 1997, Greatest Lovesongs Vol. 666 is the debut studio album by Finnish rock band HIM. Musically, the album blends heavy metal, 1980s rock, and gothic influences, creating a sound that helped define the band’s signature style—often dubbed "love metal." The lyrics center on themes of love, death, and longing, delivered with a mix of melancholy and theatricality. Produced by Hiili Hiilesmaa, the album features the only writing credits from guitarist Mikko "Linde" Lindström in the band’s history and is their only release to include keyboardist Antto Melasniemi and drummer Juhana "Pätkä" Rantala.

Greatest Lovesongs Vol. 666 established HIM’s presence in the rock world, setting the stage for their later international success. The album includes notable tracks such as "Your Sweet Six Six Six," "Wicked Game" (a cover of Chris Isaak’s hit), and "When Love and Death Embrace," which became fan favorites and helped the band gain recognition both in Finland and abroad. It reached No. 4 on the Finnish charts and achieved platinum status there, while also charting in Germany. The album’s unique blend of romanticism and darkness, along with its conceptual touches—such as hidden tracks and a runtime of exactly 66 minutes and 6 seconds—earned it attention for its originality and ambition.
